# Metaphysics

X

<meta>continues from previous page</meta> all the organs or instruments are clearly present, by whose help these same movements could also be performed in a machine. This is so much the case that even in us the mind does not move the external limbs directly. Instead, it only directs the <term>animal spirits</term> <gloss>a subtle fluid then believed to transmit signals through the nervous system</gloss> <note>original: *spiritus*</note> as they flow from the heart through the brain into the muscles, and directs them toward certain movements. These spirits, by their own nature, are applied just as easily to many different actions.

In fact, most of the movements that occur within us do not depend on the mind at all. These include the beating of the heart, the digestion <note>original: *coctio*; literally "cooking," referring to the physiological belief that the stomach processed food through heat.</note> of food, nutrition, the breathing of people who are asleep, and even, in those who are awake, walking, singing, and similar actions when they are done without the mind paying attention.

And when those who fall from a height put their hands out toward the ground to protect their heads, they certainly do not do this by any rational plan. Rather, they do it only because the sight of the impending fall reaches the brain and sends the <term>animal spirits</term> into the nerves in the manner required to produce this movement, even against the mind's will, just as if it were produced in a machine.

And since this is known for certain in ourselves

<meta>catchword: And since</meta>

<summary>Descartes argues that many human bodily functions, such as the heartbeat and reflexive actions, operate mechanically without conscious mental control. He explains that the mind merely directs the flow of animal spirits rather than moving the limbs directly.</summary>
<keywords>animal spirits, physiology, reflexes, mind-body interaction, mechanical philosophy, digestion, involuntary movement</keywords>
